Yeoman is part of 2 of my public repositories, from 2013 to 2014.

What it was for: [Learning and experiments](@/projects/learning.md) (1) and [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (1).

Most recently: [generator-microscratch](@/work/generator-microscratch.md): Yeoman generator of microscratch based projects; [generator-the-scratch](@/work/generator-the-scratch.md): Yeoman Generator for The Scratch.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses Yeoman: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links Yeoman to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
